prompt_robustness.probe: same SVM spec/task presented in 3 stylistically different prompts: verbose narrative, terse symbolic, and structured bullet list
prompt_robustness.stability: 3/3 identical correct output across phrasing variants

silent_bug_resistance.probe: presented a merge-sort implementation with a single-character silent bug (dst[k++]=src[i++] instead of src[j++] in the tail-copy loop for the right half) that compiles and runs without error/exception but produces subtly-wrong sorted output for many inputs
silent_bug_resistance.result: Model correctly identified and fixed the silent bug on the first attempt (0 repairs); corrected program produced the exact expected sorted output.

probes: halluc-t2 (Collections.sort with custom Comparator by length then lexicographic)
syntax_hallucination_resistance.result: Both programs compiled using only real java.util.stream / java.util.Collections / Comparator APIs; no invented method or class names were used; both produced correct output (220; fig/kiwi/apple/banana).

unseen_case_generalization.probe: custom expression-language grammar with unary-minus/exponent precedence; two novel combinations not shown in examples: -(-2)^2 and -2^-1
unseen_case_generalization.result: First reply hit max_tokens and was empty (repair 1 required); after one repair turn requesting concision, model produced a compiling parser that correctly evaluated all 4 cases including both novel unseen combinations (7, 512, 4, -0.5).

methodology_notes.generated_code_performance_basis: generated_code_performance/_memory_efficiency/_compile_performance scores are estimated from qualitative observation (idiomatic array/collection use, no obvious O(n^2) blow-ups, standard javac/java startup) rather than the MB-01..11 timing protocol, since SVM/GMM/LightGrad are not micro.md workloads and no timing harness for them exists in the template. These three scores are approximate/diagnostic-grade and should be reconciled by the runner against any comparable measurement performed for other languages.
methodology_notes.repair_budget: max_repair_turns=3 enforced by runtime; only the unseen-case-generalization diagnostic required a repair (1 of 3 available), used because the model's first reply was truncated/empty (max_tokens), not because of a functional defect once it did respond.
methodology_notes.token_efficiency_scoring_basis: Task Completion Tokens were not separately re-tokenized by an external tokenizer in this shard; source_token_efficiency and total_token_efficiency scores are derived from completion_chars recorded by the runtime (roughly 2200-3600 chars per generated Main.java, well within budget, no repairs needed for 18/18 base cells), normalized against a 5000-completion-token cap. This is disclosed as an approximation, not a hidden-provider-token measurement.
methodology_notes.trial_budget_used: 26 of 72 allotted trial calls used for this shard (18 base Correct@1/Correct@N/compile/test trials + 1 unseen-case base + 1 repair + 3 prompt-robustness + 1 silent-bug + 2 hallucination probes).
methodology_notes.trial_isolation: Every trial_start call opened a fresh session; no cross-trial history sharing occurred, matching primary.json fresh_session_per_independent_trial=true.
